question: Examine the lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j})$ and $\vec{r}=(\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\mu(\hat{i}+\hat{k})$. Establish that they are skew by applying the condition for coplanarity of two lines, and hence determine the acute angle between them.
explanation:
Coplanarity Test
For the first line, $\vec{a_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$. For the second line, $\vec{a_2}=\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b_2}=\hat{i}+\hat{k}$. Two lines are coplanar if
$$\left(\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}\right)\cdot\left(\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}\right)=0$$
Here,
$$\vec{a_2}-\vec{a_1}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$$
and
$$\vec{b_1}\times\vec{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&0\\1&0&1\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}$$
Therefore,
$$(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot(\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k})=-1-1-1=-3\ne0$$
Hence, the two lines are not coplanar. Their direction vectors are also not proportional, so the lines are skew.

Angle Between the Lines
If $\theta$ is the acute angle between the lines, then
$$\cos\theta=\frac{|\vec{b_1}\cdot\vec{b_2}|}{|\vec{b_1}||\vec{b_2}|}$$
Now,
$$\vec{b_1}\cdot\vec{b_2}=1(1)+1(0)+0(1)=1$$
and
$$|\vec{b_1}|=\sqrt{2},\quad |\vec{b_2}|=\sqrt{2}$$
Thus,
$$\cos\theta=\frac{1}{2}$$
Therefore,
$$\theta=60^\circ$$

Final Result
The two lines are skew, and the acute angle between them is $60^\circ$.

options.A: The scalar triple product is $-3\neq0$, so the lines are skew; their acute angle is $60^\circ$.
options.B: The scalar triple product is $0$, so the lines are coplanar; their acute angle is $60^\circ$.
options.C: The lines are skew and perpendicular, so the acute angle is $90^\circ$.
options.D: The lines are parallel and the acute angle is $0^\circ$.
